newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Far-right Turkish group calls off Cyprus protest.
newsitem.headline: Far-right Turkish group calls off Cyprus protest.

text.p: A far-right Turkish group has called off a planned protest march on the empty Greek Cypriot town of Varosha at the weekend, the official Turkish Cypriot radio station Bayrak said on Thursday.

"The gathering has been suspended until an indefinite time in the future," the radio said. It said Turkish nationalist leaders took the decision not to protest at Varosha at a meeting on Wednesday night.

Turkish Cypriot authorities said on Wednesday they would stop the march by the rightist "Grey Wolves", which had been scheduled for Sunday. The ultra-rightists had planned to storm the fenced-off town and claim buildings as their own.
Greece denounced the march and the Turkish Cypriots' sponsor Turkey had said it did not back the protest.

Varosha, a seaside resort until the Turkish invasion in 1974, lies between the Turkish Cypriot north of the island and the Greek Cypriot south. The United Nations holds Turkey responsible for the maintenance of the status quo there.
Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash has threatened to open Varosha to Turkish Cypriot settlement if the Cypriot government in the south goes ahead with a planned missile purchase from Russia.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia backed by the military ruling in Athens at the time.

The international community, with the exception of Turkey, recognises the Greek Cypriot administration in the south as the only government on the island. The Turkish Cypriot breakaway administration in the north is only recognised by Ankara.
